target_customer: Developer teams and startups that need to share API keys, database credentials and app config across people and servers
problem: Secrets sat in dotenv files, chat and ad hoc stores, which was error prone and insecure. EnvKey offered an end-to-end encrypted store with least-privilege access that integrated in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for EnvKey Cloud, plus paid Business Self-Hosted; client code open source

founders.name: Dane Schneider
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as the only founder, bio says developer and startup guy. Prior employers and education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: End-to-end encryption with key distribution, per-user access control and cross-platform clients is hard for one developer, though built on known cryptography.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into deploy pipelines gave some lock-in, but the client was later open sourced (2022) and alternatives such as Vault, Doppler and Infisical were available, so the product was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloud providers and Vault covered the need for larger customers. No acquisition of EnvKey found. A rival's blog says the hosted service closed because of running cost, not product failure.

market_need_then: Secrets leaks from committed keys and shared dotenv files were a widely discussed developer pain in 2017 and 2018. The TechCrunch coverage of Feb 2018 framed EnvKey as a smarter store for API keys and credentials.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and technical, compares itself to dotenv files and Vault on its own site

branding.community_and_virality: Posted to Hacker News in 2017 and again as Show HN 2.0 (open source) on 2022-03-30. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and memorable name but no sourced press on the brand itself; modest developer awareness.

outcome_analysis: EnvKey was a solo founder product that went through YC in Winter 2018, later open sourced its client, and began a six month wind down of EnvKey Cloud on 2024-08-01 with shutdown set for 2025-02-01. The company's stated reason was not captured here. A rival's blog attributes the closure to the cost of running a secure hosted secrets service, which is commentary and unverified. No venture round beyond YC is documented, so failure to raise and thin unit economics are plausible but not proven.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists a $120K seed on 2018-03-05 from Y Combinator, which is the standard YC deal and a single aggregator, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Wellfound and CB Insights disagree on investor count. No dated competitor sources were read, so the list is empty (Vault, SecretHub, Keywhiz and later Infisical appear in comparisons, undated). Founded year 2017 from a secondary HN repost. Shutdown cause is from a rival's blog; the company's own explanation was not found, so exit.reason is null. Social media and merch not searched deeply.
